text:
eli: Anyone else seeing duplicate token charges when a streaming request is soft-batched and then routed to a fallback? Noticed a spike on canary-03 this morning.

maria: Yep. Customer reported it. Quick snippet from the runtime logs: 
```
2026-03-10T12:34:56Z INFO session=abc123 batch=soft batch_id=b1 tokens=120 provisional=true
2026-03-10T12:34:57Z WARN session=abc123 route=fallback batch=hard batch_id=b2 tokens=80 provisional=true
2026-03-10T12:34:58Z INFO session=abc123 final_confirm tokens=200 provisional=false
```

dan: Sounds like provisional credits are emitted by both the merged soft-batch and the fallback hard-batch before final_confirm reconciles them. Ledger treats the two provisional emissions independently and we end up double-counting until final confirm logic runs (or sometimes it never reconciles if events cross services).

sophie: Is this limited to soft-batch merge behavior or any buffered-batch + fallback path?

maria: From what I traced: the batch merger assigns a new batch_id when it coalesces inflight requests. The fallback path creates a separate batch_id and emits provisional rows with that id. Reconciliation expects a single provisional per session-window, so having two batch_ids breaks dedupe.

eli: Short-term mitigation idea: dedupe provisional ledger entries by (session_id, token_window_start, token_window_end) for a 10s grace window. Long-term: change emission semantics so only the primary route emits provisional tokens; secondaries emit an idempotency marker (tombstone) that the ledger can map back to the primary batch_id.

billing-bot: Detected 12 affected sessions in the last 24h, ~73 USD in provisional duplication (approx). Query: /billing/provisional?from=2026-03-09&to=2026-03-10 :chart_with_upwards_trend:

dan: We should instrument a new metric: provisional_emit_count by route_decision (primary/fallback/merged). Dashboard ask: show provisional vs confirmed over time with a mismatch ratio and a per-route breakdown. Also add a leaderboard for sessions that saw >1 provisional emission in a 30s window.

sophie: I'll open an RFC and a console ticket for the dashboard + alerting changes. @eli can you run a canary with the ledger dedupe rule enabled? If it suppresses duplicates we can backfill remediation. :thumbsup:

eli: On it. I'll kick off a canary this afternoon and add a debug flag to log session->batch mappings for 1h. Will post results here.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: started canary deploy 2026-03-10T17:10Z canary-id=softbatch-dedupe-1

maria: If canary passes we should run a reconciliation job to detect and refund duplicate provisional credits for affected customers, and tag them for support ops to reach out.

dan: Also update alerts: if provisional_confirm_mismatch_rate > 10% over 1h (or > 0.5% for high-volume customers) page oncall. We used to only alert on final_confirm drop which misses this earlier mismatch signal.

sophie: I'll add the alert to the PR and draft the dashboard layout (per-route pie, mismatch timeseries, top offending sessions). Will include a link to the trace (trace_id) and the ledger rows API for quick triage. :raised_hands:

eli: Thanks. After canary I'll paste the logs and the before/after provisional metrics. Hopefully a quick fix.
